title: Use an Automated Testing Tool
expectation: When run against the page, the automated validation tool MUST NOT report any errors.
procedure:
1) Run one automated validation tool of your choice against the page and confirm that it reports no errors. 
2) If errors are found, record a FAIL with a FAIL ID for each issue reported by the tool.
outcomes:
Pass = automated tool returns 0 errors

Fail = automated tool returns 1 or more errors
method: Runs the full axe-core v4.13.0 rule set (WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A & AA rulesets) against the rendered page.

title: No Blinking or Flashing
expectation: Content that blinks or flashes MUST never be used.
procedure:
1) Perform a visual inspection of the page
2) Confirm that each page contains no content that blinks or flashes.
outcomes:
Pass = content that blinks or flashes is not used

Fail = content that blinks or flashes is used
method: Detects <marquee>/<blink> elements and CSS animations/transitions with infinite iteration count as candidate blinking content; confirms visually with a short multi-frame screenshot diff.

title: Text Alternatives
expectation: All non-text content MUST provide text alternatives that provide equivalent information, context, and purpose to the user using the following techniques (as applicable): • For elements, provide the text alternative using the alt attribute • For other non-text content (i.e. role="img"), aria-label/labelledby, or visibly hidden text • For decorative elements, provide alt="" (alt null) • For other decorative non-text content, aria-hidden="true"
procedure: Using Accessibility Insights, confirm that all non-text content provides text alternatives that provide equivalent information, context, and purpose to the user AND that decorative non-text content is appropriately hidden using null alternative text or aria-hidden="true"
outcomes:
Pass = all non-text content provides text alternatives AND all decorative content is hidden correctly

Fail = some non-text content does not have text alternatives OR some decorative content is not hidden correctly

NA = non-text content is not present
method: axe-core validates alt text, aria-label/labelledby, and decorative-hiding on images, icons and other non-text content.

title: Accurate Title
expectation: An accurate and descriptive page <title> title MUST be included on every page or view.
procedure:
Use ANDI>Structures>More Details>Page Title or inspect the HTML DOM and confirm that a <title> element is present.
Verify that the page title provided is accurate and descriptive of the purpose of the page and content.
outcomes:
Pass = page title is accurate and descriptive of the page content

Fail = page title is not included OR page title is inaccurate and/or not descriptive of the page content
method: axe confirms a non-empty <title> exists; the tool also flags boilerplate/very short titles. Whether the title is truly descriptive of page purpose is a human judgment.

title: Sequential Headings
expectation: Headings MUST be implemented sequentially in order without skipping levels. (i.e., Heading 1, then Heading 2, then Heading 3 and so on). Headings of the same level may be repeated (e.g., H2, H2, H2, etc.).
procedure:
1) Open ANDI>Structures>Headings
2) View all headings instances listed below the 'Headings' tab and confirm that headings occur in sequential order without skipping levels. (i.e., Heading 1, then Heading 2, then Heading 3 and so on, no skipping numbers).
outcomes:
Pass = headings descend in single increments with no skipping

Fail = headings do not descend in single increments and levels are skipped
method: axe-core's heading-order rule flags any heading level skip.

title: Link Text In and Out of Context
requirement: Link Text In and Out of Context (INT-5-2)
expectation: Link text MUST describe the destination or purpose of every link in a way that makes the destination or purpose clear to all users when taken out of context (i.e., in a list of links for the page).  Some of the link text may be hidden via CSS provided the text left visible makes sense when taken in context of the enclosing sentence, table header(s) or preceding heading.
procedure: Bring up the list of links with ANDI and confirm link text is unique and descriptive. Links describe the destination or purpose of every link in a way that makes the destination or purpose clear to all users when taken out of context (i.e., in a list of links for the page). Some of the link text may be hidden via CSS provided the text left visible makes sense when taken in context of the enclosing sentence, table header(s) or preceding heading.
outcomes:
Pass = all link text is unique and descriptive of its purpose

Fail = link text is not unique or it is not descriptive of its purpose

NA = no links are present
method: axe validates every link has an accessible name; a custom check flags generic/ambiguous text ("click here", "read more") and links that share text but point to different destinations. Judging whether text is contextually clear still needs a human.

title: Color Contrast Ratio
expectation:
A color contrast ratio of text, informational images, and images of text to their backgrounds MUST be at least 4.5:1, except if the text is 18 point or 14 point bold or larger, where a ratio of 3:1 is then required. Text that is part of a logo is not subject to this requirement.

IF there is content that does not pass color contrast requirements, then an alternate (high-contrast) compliant style sheet must be available.
procedure:
Use a contrast analyzer to check color contrast ratio of text, and images of text to their backgrounds. Use the eye  dropper tool to check any text that is missed by the automated scan. If a failure is identified with the automated scan which seems questionable use the eye dropper tool to double check. Contrast ratio MUST be at least 4.5:1, except if the text is 18 point or 14 point bold or larger, where a ratio of 3:1 is then required.

Note: All of this information will be provided in the contrast validation tool's side panel, except for text that is not HTML text or an HTML colored background (e.g., text over a gradient image). In this case, use the color picker tool from the panel to pick samples and determine if the text fails in any places.

IF there is content that does not pass color contrast requirements, then an alternate (high-contrast) compliant style sheet must be available.
outcomes:
Pass = all text meets expected minimum contrast ratio 

Fail = all text does not meet the expected minimum contrast ratio AND an alternate style sheet is not provided.

NA = text is part of an inactive user interface component or pure decoration
method: axe-core's color-contrast engine computes the rendered contrast ratio of text against its background for every text node.

title: Contrast for Non-text UI Components
expectation: User interface components and graphical objects MUST have a contrast ration of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.
procedure: Confirm that all user interface components and graphical objects have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors including the background and other non-text objects by using the eye dropper tool in a contrast analyzer
outcomes:
Pass = all user interface components and graphical objects have a contrast ratio of 3:1 against adjacent colors

Fail = some user interface components and/or graphical objects do not have a contrast ratio of 3:1 against adjacent colors
method: No reliable automated technique exists to identify which non-text graphical objects are meaningful UI components vs. decoration, which is required before a contrast ratio can even be computed.

title: Visible Keyboard Focus
expectation: A highly visible cue MUST always be presented to indicate keyboard focus. The focus indicator must maintain a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio against the background at all times to be considered highly visible. As the user navigates, they are consistently aware of the current position of keyboard focus and the focus indicator is not obscured by any content.
procedure: Tab through the entire page and confirm that the keyboard focus indicator is always clearly visible; As the user navigates, they are consistently aware of the current position of keyboard focus and the focus indicator is not obscured by any content
outcomes:
Pass = a highly visible indication of keyboard focus is always visible during keyboard or other modes of sequential navigation interaction AND the focus indicator maintains a 3:1 contrast ratio against the background at all times AND a portion of the focus indicator is visible

Fail = a highly visible keyboard focus indicator is not visible at all times OR the focus indicator does not maintain a 3:1 contrast ratio against the background at all times
method: Tabs through all focusable elements and reads the computed outline/box-shadow style at each stop, computing its contrast ratio against the adjacent background and flagging outline:none with no visible replacement.

title: Default Tab Order
expectation: Default tab order of focusable elements MUST not be overridden; the natural order of the HTML code SHOULD match the rendered page’s logical order.
procedure: Tab through the entire page and confirm that the tab order matches the logical order of the content.
outcomes:
Pass = the focus order follows the natural order of the HTML content and the rendered page's logical order appropriately

Fail = the focus order does not follow the natural order of the HTML content and/or the rendered page's logical order appropriately
method: Flags any positive tabindex value (an explicit anti-pattern that overrides natural order). Confirming the DOM order matches the visual reading order for complex layouts still needs a human.

title: Keyboard Support
expectation: All functionality and content MUST be available to users via the keyboard only (without a mouse) without requiring specific timing of keystrokes.
procedure: Run through all use cases using keyboard only (i.e., without a mouse), confirming that all features and functionality are fully available to users.
outcomes:
Pass = all features and functionality are fully available to keyboard users

Fail = one ore more features or functionality are not fully available to keyboard users
method: A heuristic scan flags elements with click handlers that are not natively focusable and lack a role/tabindex, which are likely keyboard-inaccessible. Full functional coverage of every use case requires a manual keyboard walkthrough. Interactive checks also press Enter/Space/Arrow Down on expand/collapse controls and submenu triggers to confirm they open from the keyboard, that Tab (or the menu itself) moves focus into an opened submenu, and that role="menu" submenus close on Escape and return focus to their trigger.

title: No Keyboard Trap
expectation: If any part of the UI takes control of keyboard focus (e.g., PDF viewer or modal window) it MUST, through keyboard commands only, allow focus to return to the launching element and browser.
procedure: Run through all use cases using keyboard only (i.e., without a mouse), confirm that no UI elements take control of keyboard focus unless they also return focus.
outcomes:
Pass = no UI elements take control of keyboard focus without returning it

Fail = one or more UI elements takes control of keyboard focus and does not return it
method: Automatically tabs through the page dozens of times watching for a keyboard focus cycle that never returns to the browser chrome (a trap signature). Confirms candidates for manual double-check.

title: Don't Use onFocus or onInput Events
requirement: Don't Use onFocus or onInput Events (INT-2-1)
expectation: The onFocus and onInput events MUST not be utilized to perform any actions for the user or cause a change of context for the user that would be missed or cause confusion.
procedure: Interact with each form control and confirm that no actions take place onchange or on focus.
outcomes:
Pass = no actions are performed onChange or onFocus

Fail = one or more actions are performed onChange or onFocus
method: Static scan for inline onfocus=/oninput= HTML attributes. JavaScript-attached listeners (addEventListener) cannot be detected without executing every code path, so this is a partial signal only.

title: Fully Descriptive Control Labels
expectation:
Controls and inputs MUST have one unique label attribute that fully describes the control’s purpose, including any supplementary information that the visual presentation may also provide (e.g., related controls grouped together visually).

Some or all of a label MAY be hidden with CSS if the visual presentation provides the necessary context.
procedure:
1) In the target page, examine each control/input element
2) Verify that all control/input labels and instructions are announced by a screen reader
a. The label may be hidden via CSS for visual presentation
b.Any additional instructions should appear in the accessible description.
outcomes:
Pass = all form controls have a unique label attribute that fully describes the control purpose and any supplementary information provided by the visual presentation

Fail = one or more form controls does not have a unique label fully describing the control purpose and any supplementary information provided by the visual presentation
method: axe-core confirms every control has a non-empty accessible name (label, aria-label, aria-labelledby). Judging whether that name is fully descriptive, including implied supplementary context, is manual.

title: Content Reflow
expectation:
When viewport size is constrained to 320 CSS pixels wide:

1) There is no loss of information, meaning, or functionality and any status messages are presented in the resized viewport.
user is only required to scroll VERTICALLY to view or find the content
- EXCEPT when the content requires a two-dimensional layout for meaning like tables, maps, or diagrams.

When viewport size is constrained to 256 CSS pixels high:

1) There is no loss of information, meaning, or functionality and any status messages are presented in the resized viewport.
user is only required to scroll HORIZONTALLY to view or find the content
- EXCEPT when the content requires a two-dimensional layout for meaning like tables, maps, or diagrams.
procedure:
1) Inspect the target page
2) Activate the "Toggle device toolbar" button in the top left of the browser inspect panel.
3) Use the dropdown button at the top of the page to set device width to 320px for vertically scrolling pages
4)Examine the target page to verify that all text content is available without HORIZONTAL scrolling. Content can be displayed directly in the page, revealed via accessible controls, or accessed via direct links.

OR

1) Change width back to a minimum of 375, then change device HEIGHT to 256px for horizontally scrolling pages
2) Examine the target page to verify that all text content is available without VERTICAL scrolling. Content can be displayed directly in the page, revealed via accessible controls, or accessed via direct links.
Exception: Horizontal scrolling is allowed for the following content:
-Data tables`
-Photos
-Maps
-Charts
-Games
-UI with toolbars
outcomes:
Pass = there is not a loss of information, meaning, or functionality and only one scroll dimension is required

Fail = there is a loss of information, meaning, or functionality OR vertical and horizontal scrolling are required to view the content

NA = content is any of the following:
-Data tables
-Photos
-Maps
-Charts
-Games
-UI with toolbars
method: Playwright resizes the viewport to 320 CSS px wide and 256 CSS px high and checks scrollWidth/scrollHeight for the corresponding forced scroll direction. Content-type exceptions (tables, maps, etc.) require human judgment.

title: Keep All Content in Appropriate Regions
requirement: Keep All Content in Appropriate Regions (NAV-3-2)
expectation: All rendered content MUST be within the appropriate landmark region AND the Main landmark MUST contain all of the primary page content AND no blocks of content that repeat on multiple pages are within the Main landmark.
procedure:
Using the Accessibility Insights Landmarks tool, examine the landmark regions in the page and confirm that: 
1) All page content is within a landmark region
2) All primary page content is within the Main landmark region
3) No content that repeats on multiple pages is within the Main landmark region
outcomes:
Pass = all page content is within the appropriate landmark region

Fail = one or more blocks of page content are not within a landmark region OR the Main landmark region does not include all primary page content OR content that repeats on multiple pages is within the Main landmark region
method: axe-core's region rule flags rendered content that falls outside any landmark. Confirming the Main landmark holds only primary content (and no repeated boilerplate) is manual.

title: Redundant Landmarks Have Unique Names
expectation: If a page has multiple landmarks of the same type (e.g., Main Nav and Sub Nav), those regions MUST have unique names applied using an appropriate naming technique AND the landmark role type Must not be included in the name.
procedure:
1) Use Accessibility Insights>Adhoc Tools>Landmarks to review all of the landmark roles in the page
2) Locate any instance of two or more landmarks of the same type (e.g., Main Nav and Sub Nav)
3) Confirm that each duplicate landmark has a unique name that does not include the landmark role type in the name to help screen reader users distinguish between the two.
outcomes:
Pass = all landmark regions of the same role type have unique names applied AND the name for each does not include the role type

Fail = two or more landmark roles of the same type are present AND they do not have unique names applied OR the name of one or more region includes the role type in the name value

NA = no landmark regions of the same role type are present
method: axe-core's landmark-unique rule flags duplicate-role landmarks that share the same accessible name.

title: Name, Role, Value
expectation: All controls MUST fully describe accessibility information to assistive technology (e.g. name, role, state, value, and properties).
procedure: Interact with each control using a screen reader. Confirm that each control properly announces appropriate name, role, state, values, and properties.
outcomes:
Pass = all controls announce their appropriate name, role, state, values, and properties


Fail = one or more controls does not announce the appropriate name, role, state, value, or property
method: axe-core's broad ARIA rule set validates name, role, state and value for interactive controls (buttons, links, form fields, custom widgets). Expand/collapse controls and submenu triggers are also activated from the keyboard to confirm aria-expanded is present and actually flips to match whether the controlled content is shown.

title: Support High Contrast
expectation: All content adapts and supports the user's high contrast mode settings
procedure:
Windows: Use the search feature to search for High Contrast Mode. Activate High Contrast Mode from the settings window.

Mac: Go to System Preferences>Accessibility>Display>Invert Colors.
outcomes:
Pass = all content supports high contrast mode

Fail = some content does not support high contrast mode
method: Requires toggling an OS-level high-contrast/inverted-colors mode and visually confirming every element still renders legibly — not observable from the page DOM.

title: Unique Title
expectation: The page title MUST be unique and conform to a consistent structure among the other pages.
procedure: Verify that the page title is unique and conforms to a consistent structure among the other pages.
outcomes:
Pass = page title is unique and conforms to a consistent structure among the other pages

Fail = page title is not unique and/or it does not conform to a consistent structure among the other pages.
method: In batch/crawl mode, page titles across the audited set are compared for exact duplicates and for a consistent naming pattern (e.g. shared " | Site Name" suffix). Not applicable to a single-page audit.

title: Lang Attribute
expectation: The applicable language MUST be defined on every page, inside the html tag.
procedure:
1) Use ANDI>Structures>More Details>Page Language or use the Inspect feature in the browser (e.g. Chrome F12 dev tools) to open a view of the page HTML code
2) Locate the <html> element at the beginning of the HTML DOM
3) Confirm that the lang="" attribute is correct for the language of the page content
outcomes:
Pass = correct page language is defined

Fail = page language is not defined or the incorrect page language is defined
method: axe-core validates that <html lang> is present and set to a recognized language subtag.

title: Lang of Parts of Page
expectation: A lang attribute MUST be set on every word or phrase that is in a different language than the page’s main language.
procedure:
1) Locate any words or phrases in the page content that are in a language that is different from the language of the other content in the page. 
2) Use the Inspect feature in the browser (e.g. Chrome F12 dev tools) to open a view of the page HTML code and inspect each of these words or phrases.
3) Confirm that each of these words or phrases is wrapped in a <span> element with a lang="" attribute that is correct for the language of the word or phrase.
outcomes:
Pass = all words or pages which are in a different language than the global lang are marked up with the appropriate language

Fail = words or pages which are in a different language than the global lang are not marked up with the appropriate language

NA = no words or phrases are in a different language from the global language
method: Detecting a foreign-language phrase within otherwise same-language content requires natural-language understanding of the page's prose, not structural analysis.

title: Support Screen Readers
expectation: All features and functionality made available to users within the web application MUST be functionally supported with at least one screen reader per supported platform (i.e. JAWS for Windows desktop, VoiceOver for iOS, etc.).
procedure: Run through all use cases with each supported screen reader, confirming that all features and functionality are fully available to non-sighted users.
outcomes:
Pass = all features and functionality are fully available to non-sighted users

Fail = one ore more features or functionality are not fully available to non-sighted users
method: Requires operating every feature and use case with a real screen reader (JAWS/VoiceOver/NVDA) to confirm functional parity.

title: Alerts Read
expectation: When alerts are shown on screen (i.e., success, error, or status/informative) they MUST also be read aloud by each supported screen reader without receiving focus.
procedure: Confirm that when alerts are shown on screen (i.e., success, error, or status/informative) they are also read aloud by each supported screen reader.
outcomes:
Pass = alerts shown on screen are read aloud by each supported screen reader

Fail = alerts shown on screen are not read aloud by each supported screen reader

NA = no alerts are shown on screen
method: Confirms structurally that alert/status containers exist (role="alert"/"status" or aria-live) near where alerts are shown. Whether they are actually announced by a screen reader when triggered requires live AT testing.

title: Screen Updates Read
expectation: When the user takes an action resulting in a visual change to the screen above the focus (e.g., user entered a Visa card number and the Visa logo above the input highlights onblur), each supported screen reader MUST inform the user of this change.
procedure: When the user takes an action resulting in a visual change to the screen above the focus (e.g., user entered a Visa card number and the Visa logo above the input highlights onblur), each supported screen reader announces the change to the user.
outcomes:
Pass = visual changes to the screen above the focus are announced to the user

Fail = visual changes to the screen above the focus are not announced to the user

NA = visual changes above the focus do not occur
method: Confirming a screen reader announces a visual change above the current focus point requires live assistive-technology testing during the triggering interaction.

title: Hide from Sighted Users
procedure: Run through the page with a screen reader, confirm that content included for screen readers but to be hidden visually (e.g., hidden Headings to provide content structure that is visually implied) is reading for screen readers but not onscreen.
outcomes:
Pass = screen reader only content is read by the screen reader but hidden visually

Fail = screen reader only content is EITHER not read by the screen reader OR it is read by screen reader but not hidden visually

NA = no screen reader only content is present
method: Flags visually-hidden text implemented with display:none or visibility:hidden (which also hides it from screen readers) instead of an off-screen clipping technique, which is the specific anti-pattern this requirement guards against.

title: Hide from Screen Readers
expectation:
To hide content from screen readers (but not sighted users) the following attributes MUST be used: 
• aria-hidden="true"
• Set the tabindex="-1"
procedure: Run through the page with a screen reader, confirm that content that SHOULD be hidden from screen readers (but not sighted users) is shown on screen but not showing up for screen readers.
outcomes:
Pass = content intentionally hidden from screen reader is not read by the screen reader AND is shown visually

Fail = content intentionally hidden from screen reader is read by the screen reader

NA = no content is intentionally hidden from screen reader
method: axe-core's aria-hidden-focus rule catches the most common failure mode: a focusable element nested inside an aria-hidden="true" container. Confirming intended content is fully excluded from the accessibility tree still benefits from screen reader spot-checks.

title: Group Controls Using Fieldsets
expectation: If there is more than one distinct group of related form controls on a page, the related controls MUST be grouped programmatically. This may be done using either fieldset/legend or ARIA group role/text container. Text describing the logical grouping MAY be hidden off-screen if it isn't visually necessary.
procedure: If fieldsets or aria groups are used on the page to group more than one distinct group of related form controls, confirm that the legends/ARIA legends read properly, i.e., before each label for the controls in the given group.
outcomes:
Pass = related controls are grouped using Fieldset OR ARIA group AND the legend/ARIA legend is read correctly by screen reader

Fail = related controls are not grouped using Fieldset OR ARIA group OR they are but the legend/ARIA legend is read incorrectly or not read by the screen reader

NA = no groups of related controls are present
method: Detects groups of 2+ same-name radio/checkbox inputs that are not wrapped in a <fieldset> or an ARIA group role. Confirming the legend/group label is announced correctly in the intended reading position requires a screen reader.

title: Required Fields
expectation:
Required fields/controls MUST use the aria-required="true" attribute. They MUST also be communicated in text either at the beginning of the form or in-line.

Groups of checkboxes SHOULD not have the aria-required attribute and the required state should be indicated in text either at the beginning of the form, stating all fields are required, or in the group's fieldset legend instead.
procedure:
1) Ensure that required fields are identified visually with text at the beginning of the form or in-line.

2) Tab through each control on the page and confirm that each required form control is announced as such by each supported screen reader.
outcomes:
Pass = all required fields are marked with aria-required="true" and read correctly by a screen reader AND text is available at the top of the form or in-line

Fail = one or more required field is not marked with aria-required="true" and read correctly by a screen reader OR text is not available at the top of the form or in-line.

NA = no required fields are present
method: Cross-checks the required/aria-required="true" attribute against visible "required" indicator text near the field or at the top of the form.

title: Use aria-describedby
expectation: Helper text MUST be programmatically associated with a form control using aria-describedby="<ID of helper texts container>".
procedure: Tab through each control on the page and confirm that helper text is read after the label for each form control that has helper text.
outcomes:
Pass = all helper text is associated correctly and read by the screen reader as expected

Fail = one or more helper text instances are not associated correctly OR read by the screen reader as expected

NA = no helper text is present
method: Confirms every aria-describedby reference resolves to an existing element near the control (structural correctness). Confirming a screen reader reads that text immediately after the label still requires live AT testing.

title: Specify Input Purpose Programmatically
expectation: If an input field is used to collect information about the user and the field supports autocomplete then the input field's purpose is identified programmatically.
procedure:
1) Use the Browser inspection to inspect each input field on the page. to determine if the HTML atutocomplete or autofill attributes have been used.
2) If these attributes have been used, then they must match the type of information requested from the user.
outcomes:
Pass = there are no automated errors reported and all fields which have autocomplete or autofill defined have correct, valid values that match the requested information

Fail = one or more fields are detected which have incorrect or invalid values for autocomplete or autofill or the specified values do not match the information requested from the user.

NA = no fields with autocomplete or autofill are present
method: axe-core validates that any autocomplete token used is well-formed; a heuristic then compares the token against the field's name/id/label text (e.g. an email-looking field should carry autocomplete="email").

title: Visible and Programmatic Label Consistency
expectation: If a control's visual label differs from the programmatic/accessible name value, then the programmatic/accessible name value includes the visual label.
procedure:
1) Use the ANDI tool and select Buttons/Links from the dropdown menu.
2) Use the ANDI Output section to determine whether or not any controls have a programmatic/accessible name value that is different from the visual label.
3) For any control that has a different visual label and ANDI output, confirm that the programmatic/accessible name value includes the visual label.
4) Repeat these steps using the ANDI Focusable Elements dropdown to review form fields.
outcomes:
Pass = all controls which have a different programmatic/accessible name value and visual label have the visual label text within the programmatic/accessible name value text string

Fail = one or more control which has a different programmatic/accessible name value and visual label does not have the visual label text within the programmatic/accessible name value text string

NA = no controls which have a different programmatic/accessible name value and visual label are present
method: axe-core's label-content-name-mismatch rule flags any control whose accessible name doesn't contain its visible label text.

title: Multiple Authentication Methods
expectation: User authentication must avoid relying on a cognitive function test by providing multiple means of filling in authentication information.
procedure:
Ensure that authentication form fields allow any of the following:
-The fields allow autofill of information provided by the browser.
-Information may be pasted into the form fields.
-Biometrics can be used to sign into accounts
outcomes:
Pass: The authentication fields allow autofill of stored information from the browser OR information can be copied and pasted into the fields OR biometrics (fingerprints, facial-scan, etc.) can be used to log in.

Fail: The authentication fields do not allow autofill AND information cannot be copied and pasted into the fields AND biometrics cannot be used (i.e. none of the pass criteria methods are used). 

NA: the page does not require interaction to authenticate
method: Checks that authentication fields carry autocomplete attributes (enabling password-manager autofill) and are not blocked from paste via onpaste handlers. Biometric sign-in availability is a device/OS capability outside what a page audit can observe.

title: Use “Go” Buttons
expectation: The onBlur event MUST not be used to perform any user action, unless deemed absolutely necessary.  A "go" button is always the preferred approach in this instance.
procedure: Interact with each form control and confirm that no actions take place on blur (rather they require a go button) unless this is absolutely necessary.
outcomes:
Pass = no UI changes occur onBlur unless they are passing INT-2-3

Fail = one or more UI changes occur onBlur and INT-2-3 also fails
method: Static scan for inline onblur= handlers, which is the specific pattern this requirement discourages in favor of an explicit "Go" button. Determining if the resulting behavior is "significant" is a judgment call.

title: Warn Users in Text and With describedby
requirement: Warn Users in Text and With describedby (INT-2-3)
expectation:
If an onBlur event MUST be used to cause a "significant" change to a page, the page MUST:

1) Describe what will happen via a textual description to the user prior the control being triggered, and
2) aria-describedby="<ID OF CONTAINER OF THAT TEXT>" MUST be included within the control to ensure the screen reader users will receive the message.
procedure: Interact with each form control that uses an on blur event to cause a "significant" change to a page, the page visually describes what will happen via a textual description to the user prior the control being triggered, and that description is also read to the user after the label, on focus.
outcomes:
Pass = UI changes occur onBlur causing significant change to the page visually and the user is made aware of this change

Fail = UI changes occur onBlur causing significant change to the page visually and the user is not made aware of this change and INT-2-3 also fails
method: Where an onblur handler is present, checks whether a related aria-describedby-wired warning text exists near the control. Confirming it visually describes the outcome and is read on focus requires manual/AT confirmation.

title: Activate Only on Up Event
expectation:
Actions completed with mouse or touch input MUST not use the down-event to execute any part of the function.
-OR-
Make sure there is a way for the user to abort or undo the action.
-OR-
Allow the up-event to reverse any outcome of the preceding down-event
procedure: Confirm that there are no actions which are completed using the down-event from mouse or touch input OR that there is a way for the user to abort or undo the action OR that the up-event allows the user to reverse any outcome of the preceding down-event.
outcomes:
Pass = no actions are completed using the down event OR there is a way to abort or undo an action completed on the down-event OR the up-event allows the reversal of the preceding down-event

Fail = actions are completed using the down event AND there is not a way to abort or undo the action AND the up-event does not allow reversal of the preceding down-event
method: Static scan for inline onmousedown= handlers as a proxy for down-event-triggered actions. JavaScript-attached mousedown listeners aren't visible without executing every code path, so a manual pass on interactive components is still recommended.

title: Redundant Entry
expectation: If a page is contained within a process then information provided on the first step of the process is auto-filled in the next steps unless the information is required for security.
procedure: Review the page to determine if it is a step in a process. Ensure that if information is provided in an earlier step in this process, that information is auto-filled in later steps.
outcomes:
Pass: Information provided during the process will autofill if later steps require the same information.

Fail: Fields do not autofill when the same information has been provided on previous steps.

NA: The page does not contain any process-based functionality OR information reentry is essential or required for security.
method: Whether a multi-step process re-uses previously entered information is a business-logic/state question that requires walking through the real transaction flow.

title: In-Line Error Messaging for Screen Reader
requirement: In-Line Error Messaging for Screen Reader (INT-3-5)
expectation: When an error is detected using in-line validation, any previous role="alert" instances MUST be removed from the DOM, and role="alert" MUST be set on the container of the error_helpertext.
procedure:
Enter invalid data in a form field.

Use the screen reader to navigate away from the field and confirm that after navigating away from the field aria-invalid="true" is added to the field and error helper text is associated using aria-describedby and this information is announced by the screen reader
outcomes:
Pass = for all in-line validated fields with invalid information the screen reader announces the field as invalid and the helper text when the field receives focus

Fail = for all in-line validated fields with invalid information the screen reader does not announce the field as invalid OR the helper text when the field receives focus

NA = no forms are present
method: Statically confirms role="alert" containers and aria-describedby wiring exist around form fields. Confirming stale alerts are removed and new ones announced on live validation requires screen reader testing.

title: Use aria-invalid
expectation: The aria-invalid attribute MUST be managed programmatically, when an error is being detected aria-invalid MUST be set to true. Controls that are being validated for errors MUST include aria-invalid="true" inside the <input> field when an error is present.
procedure: Tab through each control on the page and confirm that no form controls announce as invalid if they are not invalid.
outcomes:
Pass = aria-invalid is implemented correctly and invalid fields are announced correctly by the screen reader

Fail = aria-invalid is not implemented correctly OR invalid fields are not announced correctly by the screen reader

NA = no forms are present
method: axe validates that any aria-invalid value used is well-formed. The scan deliberately does not submit forms on the live page (to avoid triggering real transactions), so confirming aria-invalid is set correctly at the moment an error actually occurs requires a manual pass.

title: In-Line Error Validation for Screen Reader
requirement: In-Line Error Validation for Screen Reader (INT-3-6)
expectation:
When an error is detected using client side validation the following MUST be programmatically accommodated:

1. set aria-invalid="true"
2. add the ID of the error helper text container to the aria-describedby attribute if present or add an aria-describedby attribute if not 

Example: aria-describedby="helpertext" changes to aria-describedby="error_helpertext helpertext".
procedure: Fill out all client-side validated form controls with invalid data, return to the top of the form, and tab through all invalid form controls with each screen reader and confirm that on focus, invalid form controls are announced as such and that the text of the error helper text is read aloud.
outcomes:
Pass = when an invalid field is encountered with a screen reader it is announced as invalid and error helper text is read aloud

Fail = when an invalid field is encountered with a screen reader it is not announced as invalid and/or error helper text is read aloud

NA = no forms are present
method: Statically checks that client-side-validated forms have an error-message container wired up (role="alert"/aria-live, referenced via aria-describedby) ready to receive validation errors. The scan does not submit forms on the live page, so confirming the live announcement on an actual invalid entry requires a manual pass.

title: Check for Errors
expectation:
All pages that accept user input MUST check for errors and allow the user to correct them through validation in-line and post-submit as detailed in INT-3-2 through INT-3-6.

Where users are prevented from submitting a form with errors, in-line validation is required but post-submit validation is not. Where users are able to submit a form with errors, post-submit validation is required.
procedure: Confirm that if a page accepts user input it also checks for errors and allows the user to correct them.
outcomes:
Pass = validation is used to find errors in user input

Fail = validation is not used to find errors in user input

NA = no forms collecting user input are present
method: Statically confirms that forms collecting required input have client-side validation scaffolding in place (no unconditional novalidate, an error-message container present). The scan does not submit forms on the live page (to avoid triggering real transactions), so confirming errors actually surface on invalid input requires a manual pass.

title: Summary Before Submit
expectation: If user input is collected across multiple pages in order to execute a transaction of some kind the user MUST be presented with a summary of the input before submitting. The user MUST be able to change input prior to final submission after reviewing.
procedure:
Examine the target page to determine whether it allows users to:

make any legal commitments or financial transactions, or

modify or delete data in a data storage system, or

Submit test responses.

If the page does allow such actions, verify that the following are true:

the user is presented with a summary of the input before submitting

user can review, confirm, and correct information before finalizing the submission
outcomes:
Pass = a summary of user input is provided prior to final submit AND the user can edit or make corrections as needed

Fail = a summary of user input is not provided prior to final submit OR the user cannot edit or make corrections as needed

NA = user input is not collected across pages to execute a transaction
method: Whether a multi-page transaction shows a pre-submit summary is a UX/business-flow question that requires walking the real transaction end to end.

title: Highlight In-Line Errors Visually
expectation: When an error is detected using in-line validation, highlight the field (e.g., with a bold red border, error icon with proper alternative text) and place error helper text near it.
procedure: Confirm that when an error is detected using in-line validation, the visual UI highlights the fields with errors (e.g., with a red border) and places error helper text above or below each one.
outcomes:
Pass = when an error is detected using in-line validation, the visual UI highlights the field and places error helper text near it

Fail = for one or more client-side validated forms when an error is detected using client side validation, the visual UI does not highlight the field or place error helper text near it

NA = no forms are present
method: Statically confirms an error-message container exists near required fields, ready to be styled/positioned as a highlight when validation runs. The scan does not submit forms on the live page, so confirming the actual visual highlight on error requires a manual pass.

title: Modal Dialog ARIA Usage
expectation: Modal dialog windows MUST have the role attribute on the modal container set to role=“dialog” AND the attribute aria-modal="true".
procedure: Confirm that when a modal dialog opens that the screen reader announces it as a dialog.
outcomes:
Pass = the modal dialog container has the role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" attributes and the modal dialog is announced as a dialog by the screen reader

Fail = the modal dialog container does not have a role="dialog" and the modal dialog is not announced as a dialog by the screen reader OR the container is missing the aria-modal="true" attribute.

NA = no modal dialog is present
method: Every element in the DOM carrying role="dialog"/"alertdialog" (even ones hidden until triggered) is checked for the required aria-modal="true" attribute. Dialogs that are constructed dynamically purely in JS after a specific interaction may be missed.

title: Modal Dialogs Have Titles
expectation: Modal dialogs MUST have aria-labelledby="id of dialog-title" where dialog-title would be the modal dialog's title (e.g., main heading in modal dialog).
procedure: Confirm that when a modal dialog pops up, the modal dialog's main heading or title is read aloud to the user.
outcomes:
Pass = when a modal dialog pops up the main heading or title is read by the screen reader

Fail = when a modal dialog pops up the main heading or title is not read by the screen reader

NA = no modal dialog is present
method: Checks that each detected dialog element has an aria-labelledby attribute pointing to an existing element.

title: Modal Dialogs Have Descriptions
expectation: Modal dialogs SHOULD have aria-describedby="dialog-desc" where dialog-desc is some helpful information that is above the first focusable element.
procedure: Confirm that when a modal dialog pops up, any helpful information that is above the first focusable element is read aloud after the modal dialog's main heading or title.
outcomes:
Pass = when a modal dialog pops up, any helpful information that is above the first focusable element is read aloud after the modal dialog's main heading or title

Fail = when a modal dialog pops up, any helpful information that is above the first focusable element is not read aloud after the modal dialog's main heading or title.

NA = no modal dialog is present OR modal dialogs do not have helpful information that is above the first focusable element
method: Checks whether each detected dialog element has an aria-describedby attribute pointing to an existing element (this attribute is a SHOULD, not a MUST).

title: Modal Dialogs Trap Focus
expectation: Modal dialogs MUST trap focus inside the modal dialog.
procedure: Confirm that focus is trapped inside all modal dialogs by cycling through headings, landmark roles, and links with each supported screen reader and confirming that focus stays within the modal dialog and doesn't move the screen behind.
outcomes:
Pass = screen reader focus is trapped inside the modal dialog and only elements which are inside the modal dialog are exposed to the screen reader

Fail = screen reader focus is not trapped inside the modal dialog OR elements which are outside the modal dialog are exposed to the screen reader

NA = no modal dialog is present
method: Confirming keyboard focus is trapped requires actually opening the dialog via its real trigger interaction and tabbing through it live.

title: Modal Dialogs Set Focus
expectation:
Modal dialogs MUST have focus set to an appropriate location based on the content presented in the modal dialog.

Where to Place Focus:
- If modal dialog has form fields place focus in first field
- If modal dialog is text only with multiple paragraphs action buttons below the text place focus on the first paragraph or heading
- If modal dialog is text only with a small amount of text (e.g. a few sentences) with action buttons place focus on the first button
- Initial focus may also be set to the modal dialog container
procedure: Confirm that when a modal dialog pops up, focus is set appropriately at the start of the modal dialog content.
outcomes:
Pass = when a modal dialog opens, focus is set to the appropriate content

Fail = when a modal dialog opens, focus is not set to the appropriate content

NA = no modal dialog is present
method: Confirming where focus lands when a dialog opens requires triggering it live and observing the resulting focus target.

title: Modal Dialogs Wrap Around
expectation: Modal dialogs MUST allow the user to move through the modal dialog's focusable elements, "wrapping around" from bottom-to-top and top-to-bottom using the <TAB> and <SHIFT>+<TAB> keyboard events.
procedure: Tab through each modal dialog and confirm that the user can move through the modal dialog's focusable elements, "wrapping around" from bottom-to-top and top-to-bottom using the <TAB> and <SHIFT>+<TAB> keyboard events.
outcomes:
Pass = focus is trapped inside the modal dialog

Fail =focus is not trapped inside the modal dialog

NA = no modal dialog is present
method: Confirming Tab/Shift+Tab wrap-around inside an open dialog requires live keyboard interaction with the triggered dialog.

title: Modal Dialog Prevent Clicks Outside
expectation: Modal Dialogs MUST prevent mouse-clicks that occur outside the modal dialog from having any effect on the modal dialog.
procedure: Click outside the modal dialog with the mouse and confirm that it has no effect on the modal dialog.
outcomes:
Pass = when clicking outside of the modal dialog the modal dialog does not close

Fail = when clicking outside of the modal dialog the modal dialog does close

NA = no modal dialog is present
method: Confirming a click outside an open dialog has no effect requires triggering the dialog live and clicking outside it.

title: Dialog Main Heading
expectation: If a heading is used in a dialog the first heading level MUST be H2 followed by appropriate heading levels.
procedure:
1) Check for the presence of a heading in the dialog
2) If a heading is used, confirm that the main heading within the dialog is an H2
outcomes:
Pass = the main heading within the dialog is an H2

Fail = the main heading within the dialog is not an H2

NA = no dialog is present OR there is not a heading within the dialog
method: Within each detected dialog element, checks whether the first heading present is an H2.

title: Dialogs Close on ESC
expectation: Dialog windows MUST have the <ESC> keyboard event set to close the dialog.
procedure: Hit ESC and confirm that the dialog closes.
outcomes:
Pass = the ESC key closes the dialog successfully

Fail = the ESC key does not close the dilaog successfully 

NA = no dialog is present
method: Confirming the Escape key closes an open dialog requires triggering it live via its real interaction.

title: Dialogs Restore Focus
expectation: Dialogs MUST restore focus to their triggering element when the dialog is closed.
procedure: After hitting <esc> to close the dialog, confirm that focus is restored to the triggering element on the page.
outcomes:
Pass = after closing the dialog focus is returned to the correct triggering element

Fail = after closing the dialog focus is not returned to the correct triggering element

NA = no dialog is present
method: Confirming focus returns to the triggering element after a dialog closes requires triggering and closing it live.

title: Target Size
expectation:
Actionable components have a minimum target size of 24x24 CSS pixels except for:

Objects with a target offset of at least 24px.
EX: A 20px width “Cancel” button has its right most edge at least 4px away from a “Submit” button placed on the right.
Inline content within a sentence or block of text.
EX: A wiki paragraph has multiple instances of hyperlinked text. Increasing the height and width of these links would impact the presentation of text and make it more difficult to read.
procedure:
Use browser inspect tool to view the CSS values under the “Computed” tab. Find the height and width properties for the component. 
Ensure that each control has a width and height greater than or equal to 24px OR 
EX: A 20px width “Cancel” button has its right most edge at least 4px away from a “Submit” button placed on the right.
outcomes:
Pass: Both height and width are greater than or equal to 24px OR less than 24px with sufficient spacing between controls.

Fail: Either the height or width is less than 24px AND the center of the control is less than 24px from another control

NA: Target is a link or button in a block of text that requires a specific presentation.
method: Computes the rendered bounding box of every interactive element and flags any smaller than 24x24 CSS px whose center is also closer than 24px to a neighboring control. The inline-text-link and fixed-spacing exceptions require a final human check.

title: Links vs. Buttons
expectation:
User interface elements defined as links (anchor elements) SHOULD behave as links and user interface elements defined as buttons SHOULD behave as buttons:
- Links reference or move the user to another location
- Buttons trigger an action or event
procedure: Inspect each button and link element and confirm that each element has a defined role which is accurate for the element's purpose implemented through correct use of native element or ARIA role.
outcomes:
Pass = all links and buttons have accurately defined roles through correct use of native elements or ARIA roles

Fail = one or more link or button element does not have an accurate role

NA = no link or button elements are present
method: Flags anchors with no href attribute (should likely be a <button>) and non-interactive elements (<div>/<span>) carrying click handlers without a button/link role. Confirming actual click-vs-navigate behavior for every control is manual.

title: Valid Link href Attribute
expectation: Links MUST contain a valid href attribute value and MUST  not point to "javascript:void(0);" nor "#".
procedure: Bring up the list of links with ANDI if available and confirm no links HREF points to "javascript:void(0);" nor "#".
outcomes:
Pass = all links contain valid href attribute values

Fail = one or more links do not contain valid href values

NA = no links are present
method: Scans every link's resolved href for the "#" or "javascript:void(0)" anti-patterns.

title: Links Opening in New Tabs
expectation: If a link opens in a new browser tab or window an aria-label AND visual cue MUST be added to inform users of this interaction.
procedure:
For each link that opens automatically in a new window or tab:

1. Confirm that there is an aria-label informing users that this link opens to a new window.

2. Check that there is a visual cue in text that this link opens to a new window.
outcomes:
Pass = all links which open in a new window or tab have an aria-label and visual cue informing users of this interaction

Fail = one or more links which open in a new window or tab do not have an aria-label OR visual cue informing users of this interaction

NA = no links open in a new window or tab
method: Flags every target="_blank" link and checks whether it carries an aria-label/visible text mentioning "new window/tab". Judging whether an accompanying icon is a sufficient visual cue is manual.

title: Click and Drag Movements
expectation:
An action that relies on clicking and dragging of content can also be achieved by a single pointer without dragging unless dragging is essential to the activity.

Example of single pointer Pass: A quiz relies on users clicking and dragging information into the correct bucket. Users are also able to click once to select an option, then click on the correct bucket.
Example of essential activity: A medical app requires clicking and dragging an object to a target to accurately measure the user’s precision.
procedure: Visually inspect the page to determine whether any functionality requires a user to click and move their mouse to access content.
outcomes:
Pass: All click and drag functionality can also be performed with a single pointer OR the dragging movement is essential.

Fail: Click and drag functionality cannot be completed with a single pointer.

NA: The page does not contain click and drag functionality.
method: Confirming a drag interaction has a single-pointer (click-based) alternative requires manually operating the actual drag-and-drop widget.

title: Flexible Orientation
expectation: Content MUST adapt to the device orientation when orientation is changed from portrait to landscape unless a specific orientation is required for use of the page.
procedure:
Set display orientation to each orientation mode (portrait and landscape) and review how the content responds. 
This can be done using OS settings (Start>Settings>System>Display) or inspecting the page in your browser and using the device list to change orientations.
outcomes:
Pass = Content adapts to all display orientations

Fail=Content does not adapt to all display orientations

NA =A specific display orientation is essential (e.g. bank check)
method: Playwright renders the page at matching portrait and landscape viewport dimensions and flags new horizontal overflow or clipped content introduced by the rotation. Whether a fixed orientation is genuinely essential to the content is a judgment call.

title: Pause, Stop, Hide Moving Content
expectation:
A mechanism MUST be provided to pause, stop, or hide any content that meets the following criteria:

• Starts automatically
• Is presented in parallel with other content
AND
• moves, blinks or scrolls for >5 seconds
OR 
• All auto-updating content regardless of duration
procedure:
1) Perform a visual inspection of the page
2) Confirm that for any content that meets the following criteria, a mechanism is provided to pause, play, or hide the applicable content:
• Starts automatically
• Is presented in parallel with other content
AND
• moves, blinks or scrolls for >5 seconds
OR 
• All auto-updating content regardless of the time of duration
outcomes:
Pass = a mechanism is provided to pause, stop, or hide auto-playing; moving or blinking; auto-updating content

Fail = a mechanism is not provided to pause, stop, or hide auto-playing; moving or blinking; auto-updating content

NA = no auto-playing; moving or blinking; auto-updating content is present
method: Detects <marquee>, CSS animations with an infinite iteration count, and autoplaying <video>/animated content, then checks for a nearby pause/stop control referenced by an aria-label.

title: Pause or Adjust Volume for Auto Playing Audio
requirement: Pause or Adjust Volume for Auto Playing Audio (INT-6-2)
expectation:
For any audio which 1) plays automatically and 2) lasts for >3 seconds, ONE of the following MUST be true:

• A mechanism to pause the content is presented to the user
OR
• A mechanism for adjusting the volume of the content is presented to the user AND it does not rely on the system audio levels to adjust the volume.
procedure:
Confirm that for any audio which 1) plays automatically and 2) lasts for >3 seconds, ONE of the following is true:
• A mechanism to pause the content is presented to the user.
OR
• A mechanism for adjusting the volume of the content is presented to the user AND it does not rely on the system audio levels to adjust the volume.
outcomes:
Pass = for all content which plays automatically and lasts for more than 3 seconds a mechanism is provided to pause OR adjust volume

Fail = a mechanism is not provided to pause OR adjust volume for all content which plays automatically and lasts for more than 3 seconds 

NA = no content which plays automatically and lasts for more than 3 seconds is present
method: Detects autoplaying <audio>/<video> elements and checks whether they are muted or expose native/custom controls for pausing or adjusting volume.

title: Warn About Timeout
expectation: Users MUST be warned prior to when a session times out and expires.
procedure: Visual Inspection
outcomes:
Pass = session timeout warning occurs prior to session time out and expiration

Fail = session timeout occurs without warning

NA = no session timeout is present
method: Session-timeout warning behavior only surfaces after waiting out a real session on the live application and cannot be exercised from a static or single-pass page audit.

title: Extend Timeout
expectation: Users MUST be given at least 30 seconds to take action in order to avoid a session time out by extending the time limit (of a session) via a "simple" user action (e.g., "press the space bar").
procedure: Confirm that users are given at least 30 seconds to take action in order to avoid a session time out by extending the time limit (of a session) via a "simple" user action (e.g., "press the space bar").
outcomes:
Pass = users are given at least 30 seconds to extend the session via a simple user action

Fail = users are given less than 30 seconds to extend the session via a simple user action

NA = no session timeout is present
method: Confirming the minimum 30-second timeout-extension window requires exercising a real timing-based session on the live application.

title: Motion Control
expectation: If functionality can be operated or activated by device or user motion then it can also be operated or activated through UI components AND motion actuation can be turned off to avoid unintentional activation by the user.
procedure: For all functionality that can be operated or activated by moving the device or user motion input confirm that the same functionality can be operated or activated through UI components AND confirm that the motion actuation can be turned off by the user
outcomes:
Pass = all functionality that can be operated or activated by device or user motion has a UI control alternative AND motion actuation can be turned off by the user

Fail = any aspect of functionality that can be operated or activated by device or user motion does not have a UI control alternative OR motion actuation cannot be turned off by the user

NA = no functionality that can be operated or activated by device or user motion is present
method: Device/user motion actuation can only be exercised with a physical device's motion sensors, which a browser-based audit cannot simulate.

title: Mouse Hover and Keyboard Focus are Equivalent
requirement: Mouse Hover and Keyboard Focus are Equivalent (NAV-1-2)
expectation: Content which is hidden until it receives mouse hover and then becomes visible MUST also be shown when it receives keyboard focus and hidden again when focus is removed.
procedure:
1) Run through all use cases using the keyboard only (i.e., without a mouse) 
2)Confirm that any mouse hover events are also available to the keyboard when the keyboard focus is placed on the element.
outcomes:
Pass = all mouse hover events are also available to the keyboard when the keyboard focus is placed on the element

Fail = one or more mouse hover events are not available to the keyboard when the keyboard focus is placed on the element

NA = mouse hover events are not present
method: Scans stylesheets for :hover selectors that alter visibility/display of content, then programmatically focuses the same trigger element and compares computed style to confirm the same content also appears on keyboard focus. Navigation submenus without ARIA are hovered with the mouse and then focused with the keyboard to confirm a submenu that appears on hover also appears (and is reachable) on keyboard focus.

title: Content on Hover or Focus
expectation: For tooltips and components that show hidden content when they receive keyboard or pointer focus and hidden after removal of focus ensure they are dismissible, hoverable, and persistent.
procedure:
1) Use the keyboard to navigate to all tooltips and components that show hidden content when they receive keyboard or pointer focus and hide it after removal of focus 
2) ensure they are dismissible, hoverable, and persistent.
outcomes:
Pass = all of the hover show/hide content is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent

Fail =  hover show/hide content is not all dismissible, hoverable, and persistent

NA = no  hover show/hide content is present
method: Flags elements relying on the native title="" attribute for supplementary content, since native tooltips are not dismissible, hoverable, or reliably persistent as this requirement demands.

title: Pointer and Multipoint Gestures
expectation: An action that is performed by a 'path-based gesture' or multipoint gesture MUST also be completable using a single pointer gesture and a keyboard or alternative input device.
procedure:
1. Use the keyboard to navigate to all path-based or multipoint gesture operable controls and confirm that they can all be operated with keyboard control 

2. Use the mouse to interact with all path-based or multipoint gesture operable controls and confirm that they can all be operated with a single pointer gesture control as well.
outcomes:
Pass = all actions that can be performed by a path-based or multipoint gesture can also be completed with a keyboard and a single pointer gesture (individual mouse clicks)

Fail = one or more actions that can be performed by a path-based or multipoint gesture cannot be completed with a keyboard OR a single pointer gesture (individual mouse clicks)

NA = no actions that can be performed by a path-based or multipoint gesture are present
method: Confirming a path-based or multipoint gesture has a working single-pointer/keyboard alternative requires manually operating the real gesture-driven component.

title: Skip to Main Content Link
expectation: A "skip to main content" link MUST be included on every page as the first link (or second if "skip to login" link is present) on the page. The link MUST skip to the main content of the page or the errors summary if present and may be visually hidden until it has focus.
procedure:
Tool: Keyboard

Hit Tab after the page loads. Confirm that the first or second link on the page is "skip to main content" - it may be visibly hidden until it receives focus. If running the test on a Single Page Application (SPA) refresh the page and confirm that the first or second link is "Skip to main content"
outcomes:
Pass = a skip to main content link is provided and it is fully operational

Fail = a skip to main content link is not provided OR the skip to content link is not fully operational
method: Checks that the first (or second, after a "skip to login" link) link in the page's tab order is a working skip link whose target element exists in the DOM.

title: No Access Keys
expectation: Access keys MUST not be used.
procedure: Confirm that no accesskeys are used on the page.
outcomes:
Pass = no accesskeys are used

Fail = accesskeys are used
method: Scans the full DOM for any accesskey attribute, which this requirement prohibits outright.

title: Single Character Keyboard Shortcuts
expectation:
If a single character shortcut is used then users MUST have the option to either turn it off or remap it to one or more non-printable keyboard characters.
-OR-
Make sure the single character shortcut is only active when the component it affects has focus.
procedure:
Confirm that where a single character shortcut is used that users have the option to either turn it off or remap it to one or more non-printable keyboard characters.
-OR-
Make sure the single character shortcut is only active when the component it affects has focus.
outcomes:
Pass = for all single character shortcuts, users have the option to either turn off or remap it to one or more non-printable keyboard characters OR the single character shortcut is only active when the component it affects has focus.

Fail = for all single character shortcuts, users do not have the option to either turn off or remap it to one or more non-printable keyboard characters AND the single character shortcut is active at all times.

NA = no single character shortcuts are present
method: Detecting single-character keyboard shortcuts requires analyzing every JavaScript keydown listener's runtime behavior, which cannot be determined from the static DOM.

title: Disabled Control Focus
expectation:
When a form field or control is disabled it SHOULD not receive keyboard focus. Doing this reinforces 1.4.1 Use of Color so that the only means of conveying that a control is disabled doesn't rely solely on color (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html).

List of Composite Control Exceptions:
- Options in a List box
- Menu items in a Menu or menu bar
- Tab elements in a set of Tabs
- Tree items in a Tree View
procedure: Tab through the entire page and confirm that disabled elements do not receive visible keyboard focus unless the control is listed in the exceptions list
outcomes:
Pass = keyboard focus does not move to any disabled elements other than those which are included in the list of composite control exceptions

Fail = keyboard focus does move to one or more disabled elements which are not included in the list of composite control exceptions

NA = no disabled elements are present
method: Tabs through every element in the page and flags any disabled/aria-disabled="true" element that still receives keyboard focus, outside the listed composite-widget exceptions (listbox options, menu items, tabs, tree items).

title: Appropriate Use of Landmark Regions
expectation: The page MUST have a 'Main' landmark region defined at a minimum and Banner, Navigation, Search, Complementary, and ContentInfo roles are present if these content types are present in the page.
procedure:
1) Open the page in the Chrome browser and use Accessibility Insights>Adhoc Tools>Landmarks  to visualize the landmark regions that are present in the page. 
2) Confirm that the page has a 'Main' landmark region defined at a minimum. 
3) Confirm that the Banner, Navigation, and ContentInfo roles are present if these content types are present in the page.
outcomes:
Pass = the page contains a main landmark region AND if content suited for a navigation, banner, or contentinfo region is present then the appropriate roles are applied to each content area respectively

Fail = the page does not contain a main landmark region OR content suited for a navigation, banner, or contentinfo region is present AND the appropriate roles are not 
applied to each content area respectively

NA = the page content is not substantial enough to be grouped in one or more landmark regions
method: axe-core's landmark rule set confirms a Main landmark is present and that Banner/Navigation/ContentInfo regions are correctly structured where used.

title: Consistent Context Cues
expectation:
The following MUST be consistent on each page: 
• Page title
• Current Navigation menu item
• Progress Indicator / Wizard Step (if present)
• Top-level heading (H1)
• referring link (if present)
procedure:
Confirm that the following are consistent on each page:

Page title

Current Navigation menu item

Progress Indicator / Wizard Step (if present)

Top-level heading (H1)

referring link (if present)
outcomes:
Pass = context cues are consistent on each page

Fail = one or more context cues are not consistent on each page
method: In batch/crawl mode, compares page title pattern, current-nav-item highlighting, H1 text, and progress-indicator text across the audited pages for consistency. Not applicable to a single-page audit.

title: More Than One Way to Find Content
requirement: More Than One Way to Find Content (NAV-4-5)
expectation:
Users MUST be provided more than one way to find content within a website except when the web page is the result of a step or process. This provision MUST include two or more of the following navigational methods:
• Links to navigate to related Web pages
• a Table of Contents
• a Site Map
• a search function 
• a list of links to all other Web pages
• Linking to all of the pages on the site from the home page
procedure:
1) Review the page and site navigation structure
2) Confirm that the site provides at least 2 of the following ways to find content:
-Links to navigate to related Web pages
-Table of Contents
-Site Map
-Search function
-List of links to all other Web pages
-Linking to all of the pages on the site from the home page
outcomes:
Pass = the site provides 2 or more ways to find content

Fail = the site provides fewer than 2 ways to find content
method: Detects the presence of a <nav> region, a search form/input, and a link whose text or href suggests a sitemap, then counts how many distinct "find content" methods are present.

title: Same Relative Order
expectation: Components, like links, buttons, or contact forms, that appear on multiple pages MUST appear in the same relative order on every page.
procedure:
1) Perform a visual inspection of the page looking for navigation components
2) Confirm that components (links, buttons, contact forms, etc.) that appear on multiple pages appear in the same relative order on every page.
outcomes:
Pass = components that appear on multiple pages appear in the same relative order on every page

Fail = one or more component that appears on multiple pages does not appear in the same relative order on every page

NA = no component appears on multiple pages
method: In batch/crawl mode, compares the relative DOM order of repeated header/nav/footer components across the audited pages. Not applicable to a single-page audit.

title: Name Consistently
expectation: Consistent labels, names, and text alternatives MUST be used for content that has the same functionality.
procedure: Confirm that content with the same functionality has consistent labels, names, and text alternatives.
outcomes:
Pass = content with the same functionality has consistent labels, names, and text alternatives

Fail = content with the same functionality does not have consistent labels, names, or text alternatives

NA = no content with the same functionality is present
method: In batch/crawl mode, groups elements that share the same href/action across pages and compares their accessible names for consistency. Judging whether two controls truly share "the same functionality" is manual.

title: Consistent or Unique Link Text
expectation: Links with the same HREF MUST have the same link text and vice versa, and links with different HREFs MUST have different link text and vice versa.
procedure:
1) Use ANDI or the browser inspect feature to inspect each <a> link element in the page/view
2) Review the HREF (URL) of all links and: 
a. confirm that links with the same HREF have the same link text
b. confirm that links with different HREFs have different link text and vice versa.
outcomes:
Pass = all links with the same HREF have the same link text and vice versa; and links with different HREFs have different link text and vice versa.

Fail = one or more links with the same HREF do not have the same link text and vice versa; and/or links with different HREFs do not have different link text and vice versa.

NA = no links with the same HREF are present
method: Builds a map of href → link text (and vice versa) for the page and flags any href reused with different text, or identical text pointing to different destinations.

title: Pagination is Navigation
expectation: Pagination controls MUST have the attribute role="navigation".
procedure:
1) Locate any 'pagination' controls in the page content
2) Switch on the Accessibility Insights landmark tool
3) Confirm that any pagination controls on the screen have role="navigation".
outcomes:
Pass = all pagination controls have have role="navigation"

Fail = one or more pagination controls do not have role="navigation"

NA = no pagination controls are present
method: Heuristically identifies pagination controls (numbered page links, "next/previous" patterns, class/aria-label containing "pagination") and checks for role="navigation".

title: Label Pagination
expectation: Pagination controls MUST have the attribute aria-label="Pagination". If there are more than one pagination controls on a page, they MUST have unique labels, but still contain the word "Pagination".
procedure: Cycle through each landmark role with each supported screen reader and confirm that any pagination controls have the word "Pagination" included in their aria-label.
outcomes:
Pass =  all pagination controls have "Pagination" included in their aria-label

Fail = one or more pagination controls does not have "Pagination" included in its aria-label

NA = no pagination controls are present
method: For each heuristically-detected pagination control, checks whether its aria-label includes the word "Pagination".

title: Wizard Context Provided
expectation: Process or Wizard Step Indicators MUST provide context and status to screen readers (e.g., "Current Step: Add Card, Step 2 of 4").
procedure: Read any process or Wizard Step Indicators with screen reader and confirm it provides context and status to screen readers (e.g., "Current Step: Add Card, Step 2 of 4").
outcomes:
Pass = the process / wizard step indicator provides context and status to screen readers

Fail = the process / wizard step indicator does not provide context or status to screen readers

NA = no process / wizard step indicators are present
method: Confirming a screen reader announces step context and status for a wizard indicator requires live assistive-technology testing.

title: Wizard Info in Title/H1
expectation: Any Process or Wizard Step Indicator information MUST be included in the page title and H1.
procedure: Confirm that any process or wizard step indicator information, if present, is included in the page title and H1.
outcomes:
Pass = any process or wizard step indicator information is included in the page title and H1

Fail = any process or wizard step indicator information is not included in the page title and/or H1

NA = process or wizard step indicator information is not present
method: Detects step-indicator text patterns (e.g. "Step 2 of 4") and checks whether the same text appears in the page <title> and H1.

title: Use Headings
expectation: Pages MUST organize content using headings (e.g., H1, H2, etc.) AND the headings must accurately describe their sub-content.
procedure:
1) Open ANDI > Structures > Headings > View Headings List
2) View all headings instances listed below the 'View headings list' button
3) Confirm that each page organizes content using headings (e.g., H1, H2, etc.) and that all content which serves as a heading visually and structurally is also exposed as a heading programmatically.
4) Confirm that the page headings accurately describe their sub-content
outcomes:
Pass = headings are used AND they accurately describe their sub-content

Fail = headings are not used OR they do not accurately describe their sub-content

NA = there is not sufficient content to warrant the use of headings
method: axe-core confirms headings are structurally well-formed (no skipped levels, no empty headings) and that content is organized with real heading elements rather than styled text. Judging whether each heading accurately describes its sub-content is manual.

title: Use a Single Descriptive H1
expectation: Each page MUST have only one H1 which is descriptive of the overall page topic/purpose. The H1 and the page title SHOULD be similar and consistent.
procedure:
1) Open ANDI > Structures >  Headings > View Headings List
2) View all headings instances listed below the 'View Headings List' button and confirm that there is a single H1 in the list
3) Confirm that the H1 is descriptive of the overall page topic/purpose
4) Confirm that the H1 and page title are similar and consistent
outcomes:
Pass = there is only one H1 level heading present AND it is descriptive of the page topic/purpose AND similar similar to the page title

Fail = there are two or more H1 level headings present OR the H1 is not descriptive of the page topic/purpose OR not similar to the page title
