method: Counts H1 elements on the page (flagging zero or multiple) via axe's page-has-heading-one rule plus a direct count. Judging whether the single H1 is descriptive and consistent with the page title is manual.

title: H1 at Top of Main
expectation: The H1 MUST be within and at the top of the Main ARIA Landmark, with no plain text content (i.e. <div> or <span>) above it.
procedure:
1) Run ANDI>Structures>Headings
2) find the H1 outlined on the page and confirm that the H1 is within and at the top of the Main ARIA Landmark (also outlined), with no plain text content (i.e. <div> or <span>) above it.
outcomes:
Pass = H1 is within and at the top of the Main ARIA Landmark, with no plain text content above it

Fail = H1 is not within and at the top of the Main ARIA Landmark OR there is plain text content above it
method: Locates the Main landmark and the page's H1, then checks that the H1 is the first meaningful content inside Main with no preceding text nodes.

title: Paragraph Markup for Text
expectation: Paragraphs MUST be marked up as paragraphs.
procedure:
1) Determine whether or not the page contains paragraphs of text by scanning the page visually. 2) If paragraphs of text are present, pull up the source code with the browser inspect feature (e.g. Chrome F12 Dev tools) and confirm that those paragraphs are marked up properly with the HTML

element.
outcomes:
Pass = all paragraph text is marked up as

element Fail = all paragraph text is not marked up as

element
method:
Flags likely pseudo-paragraphs — runs of text separated by

rather than wrapped in

elements.

title: Group Items with Lists
expectation: Groups of items (e.g., a navigation menu or group of tabs) MUST be marked up as a list.
procedure:
1) Locate any text content that is presented in a list format such as bulleted or numbered lists.
2) Locate any groups of items that should be marked up as lists (e.g., a navigation menu or group of tabs) 
3) Use the browser inspect feature to examine the HTML for these list components and confirm that they are properly marked up as lists.
outcomes:
Pass = all groups of items are marked as lists

Fail = all groups of items are not marked as lists

NA = no groups of items are present
method: Flags groups of 3+ visually-repeated sibling elements (e.g. a run of <a> tags forming a menu) that are not wrapped in a <ul>/<ol>/<dl>.

title: Use Correct Semantic Markup
expectation: Whenever content conveys information through presentation of text, appropriate semantic markup (e.g., em, strong, cite, blockquote, sub, and sup) MUST be used.
procedure:
1) Locate any text content that is visually styled as bold, citation, blockquote, or other text styles.
2) Use the browser inspect feature to examine the HTML for text with visual styling.
3) Confirm that wherever content conveys information through visual style  of text  appropriate, semantic HTML markup is being used (e.g., em, strong, cite, blockquote, sub, and sup).
outcomes:
Pass = all text content has semantic markup applied appropriately

Fail = some text content does not have semantic markup applied correctly
method: Flags presentational <b>/<i> elements, which usually should be <strong>/<em> when they convey emphasis or importance rather than pure styling.

title: Code Order = Logical Content Order
expectation: The logical order of content MUST be present in the code order, allowing for successful use of the content when linearized and/or without CSS.
procedure:
1) Open the WAVE tool with the page you are testing open in your browser.
2) Use the toggle switch to 'Disable styles'.
3) Confirm that the logical order of content is present in the code order.
outcomes:
Pass = the logical order of the content is followed

Fail = the logical order of the content is not followed
method: Compares each element's DOM order position against its rendered top-to-bottom, left-to-right visual position (bounding-box order) and flags large divergences, approximating the WAVE "disable styles" technique.

title: Remove or Park “Hidden” Content at the Bottom
requirement: Remove or Park “Hidden” Content at the Bottom (TXT-3-2)
expectation: "Hidden" content being "parked" for later use/display (e.g., the text to be used by a JS calendar picker) SHOULD be removed from the DOM if possible, and if not it SHOULD be placed at the bottom.
procedure:
1) Open the WAVE tool with the page you are testing open in your browser.
2) Use the toggle switch to 'Disable styles'.
3) Confirm that "hidden" content being "parked" for later use/display is located at the bottom of the document.
outcomes:
Pass = all "hidden" content being "parked" for later use/display is located at the bottom of the DOM

Fail = some "hidden" content being "parked" for later use/display is not located at the bottom of the DOM

NA = no "hidden" content being "parked" for later use/display is present
method: Finds elements hidden via display:none/visibility:hidden (and not marked aria-hidden) and checks whether they are positioned near the end of the document body as this requirement recommends.

title: Instructions Don’t Rely on Visual Cues
requirement: Instructions Don’t Rely on Visual Cues (TXT-4-1)
expectation: Instructions MUST never refer solely to visual cues such as size, shape, color, or spatial directions.
procedure:
1) Review any instruction text (on-screen and screen reader only)
2) Confirm that Instructions and interactions never refer solely to visual cues such as size, shape, color, or spatial directions.
outcomes:
Pass = instructions and interactions never refer solely to visual cues such as size, shape, color, or spatial directions

Fail = instructions and interactions refer solely to visual cues such as size, shape, color, or spatial directions

NA = no instructions  are present
method: Judging whether instructional text relies solely on a visual/spatial cue ("click the round, red button") requires reading comprehension of free-form prose that cannot be reliably pattern-matched.

title: Instructions Include Labels as Cues
expectation: Text labels and/or names MUST be used when providing instructions to allow users who cannot perceive other indicators to locate elements.
procedure: Confirm that text labels and/or names are used when providing instructions to allow users who cannot perceive other indicators to locate elements.
outcomes:
Pass = where on-screen instructions refer to elements with labels, those labels are included in the instructions

Fail =  where on-screen instructions refer to elements with labels, those labels are not included in the instructions

NA =  on-screen instructions do not refer to elements with labels; no on-screen instructions are present
method: Confirming that on-screen instructions reference elements by their actual accessible label text requires cross-referencing free-form prose against the page's controls, a task better suited to human review.

title: No Layout Tables
expectation: Tables MUST not be used for layout purposes. Layout tables are not a direct WCAG 2.0 AA failure, however when a table is linearized it can complicate or confuse the linear order of the content (See WCAG F49 for details).
procedure:
1) Run the ANDI tool on the page.
2) Locate any table elements identified by ANDI on the page.
3) Confirm that none of the tables are used for layout purposes.
outcomes:
Pass = tables are not used for layout positioning; CSS is used instead

Fail = one or more layout table(s) is used
method: Flags <table> elements that contain no <th> and no <caption>, a strong heuristic signature of a layout table rather than a data table.

title: Markup Tables
expectation: All data tables MUST use THs and every TH MUST have scope="col" or "row" set unless any implied relationships would be untrue.  In that case, headers= MUST be used to hard code how headers are read to users.
procedure:
1) Run the ANDI tool on the page.
2) Locate any table elements identified by ANDI on the page.
3) Confirm that <th> elements are used as appropriate and every <th> element has scope as appropriate. If present, confirm that headers point to the correct <th> elements' IDs.
outcomes:
Pass = tables have correct <th> elements, <td> elements, and scope applied appropriately

Fail = one or more tables does not have correct <th> elements, <td> elements, and scope applied appropriately

NA = no tables are present
method: axe-core validates that data cells are associated with header cells and that scope/headers attributes are used correctly.

title: Identify Tables
expectation:
Data tables MUST be identified for screen readers by including the "title" of the table in its <caption> element, e.g., "Transaction History for x2304".
Note: The caption may be hidden visually with CSS.
procedure: Bring up the list of tables (or cycle through each if a list is not available) with each supported screen reader and confirm that each table is identified.
outcomes:
Pass = all tables have titles that are read by the screen reader

Fail = one or more tables does not have a title that is read by the screen reader

NA = no tables are present
method: Checks every <table> for a <caption> element. Judging whether the caption text is an accurate title is manual.

title: Summarize Table Layout
expectation:
If a data table has more than 4 table headings (THs), the layout/functionality of the table MUST be described in the caption after the "title" of the table. (E.g., Transaction History for x2304: recent transactions in column 1 and details in the next 4 columns. Actions for each transaction are available in column 6.”)
Note: The caption may be hidden visually with CSS.
procedure: Bring up the list of tables (or cycle through each if a list is not available) with each supported screen reader and confirm that each table with more than 4 THs has its layout/functionality described after the "title".
outcomes:
Pass = all complex tables have summaries of layout and functionality and screen reader announces the information

Fail = all complex tables do not have summaries of layout and functionality OR screen reader does not announces the information

NA = no complex tables are present
method: Counts <th> elements per table; for tables with more than 4, checks whether the caption includes additional descriptive text beyond a short title (a proxy for a layout/functionality summary).

title: Summarize Table Layout
expectation: Pages MUST be coded to allow users to increase the font size of all page content without text clipping, truncating, or being obscured.
procedure:
Windows OS: Use the Windows key and type "Make Text size bigger"

MacOS: Display settings>Larger Text

Use the OS settings to increase text size to 200% and confirm that text on the target page adapts and is not clipped, truncated, or obscured.
outcomes:
Pass = all text adapts to Very Large font size setting and is visible without clipping truncation, or overlapping other text.

Fail = Some text does not adapt to Very Large font size setting and/or text clipping, truncation, or overlap occurs.
method: Simulates a 200% OS-level text-size increase by scaling root font-size, then checks for resulting horizontal overflow or clipped/truncated text (fixed-height containers with overflow:hidden).

title: Browser Zoom Usable
expectation: Using the built-in browser functionality to zoom all page content to 200% (including text), all interactive content MUST remain fully usable.
procedure: Use browser zoom to magnify your viewport to 200% and confirm that all interactive content remains fully usable.
outcomes:
Pass = all interactive content remains fully usable up to 200% 

Fail = some interactive content does not remain fully usable between 0 - 200%
method: Emulates 200% browser zoom (halving the effective viewport at a 1280px baseline) and checks for horizontal scrollbars, overlapping elements, or interactive controls pushed outside the viewport.

title: Browser Zoom - Informed of Changes
expectation:
Using the built-in browser functionality to zoom all page content to 200% (including text), any user actions that result in on-screen changes MUST meet one of the following criteria:
• A clear visual cue is provided within the viewed area that indicates to the user that the page has changed outside of the currently viewed area based on their action.
• The resulting change occurs within the currently viewed area.
procedure:
Using the browser's built in functionality, set the browser to a width of 1280px and then increase the zoom level to 200% and confirm that when an action is initiated that results in changed content:
1) clear visual cue is provided within the currently viewed area indicating a change has occurred outside of currently viewed area OR
2) the resulting change can be observed within the current view.
outcomes:
Pass = changes of content resulting from user action are accompanied with a clear visual cue within the user's zoomed in view to notify the user OR the changes are visible within the user's zoomed in view

Fail = changes of content resulting from user action are accompanied with a clear visual cue within the user's zoomed in view to notify the user OR the changes are visible within the user's zoomed in view

NA = no changes of content resulting from user action occur
method: Confirming that a user-triggered content change is either visible within, or clearly signalled from, the current 200%-zoomed viewport requires performing the real triggering interaction and observing the result live.

title: User Text Styling
procedure:
1) Load the page in the browser of your choice.
2) Run the Text Spacing Bookmarklet
3) Perform a visual inspection of the content and confirm that there is not a resulting loss of content or meaning.
outcomes:
Pass = there is not a resulting loss of content or meaning when any of the four text spacing settings are changed

Fail = there is a loss of content or meaning when the four text spacing settings are changed
method: Injects the WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing values (line-height 1.5x, paragraph-spacing 2x, letter-spacing 0.12x, word-spacing 0.16x) via CSS and checks for resulting overflow or clipped content.

title: Not Only Color
expectation:
If a color difference is used to convey information, that information MUST also be available in text or through some other alternative method.

Link text may be distinguished from static text through use of color as long as the following are true:

- A 3:1 contrast ratio difference exists between the link text and other static text
- A visual indicator is provided when the link receives focus (e.g. visible underline on hover and keyboard focus)
procedure:
1) Perform a visual inspection of the page 
2) Confirm that whenever a difference in color is used to convey information, that information is also be available in text or through some other alternative method.
outcomes:
Pass = a non-color alternative is presented along with color

Fail = only color is used to indicate meaning 

NA = color is not used to convey meaning
method: axe-core's link-in-text-block rule confirms links within body text remain distinguishable without relying on color alone. Other color-only-meaning patterns (e.g. red-only form errors) require visual review.

title: No Images of Text
expectation: Text MUST always be presented using live text and CSS rather than an image of text, except for logos and within pictures where it cannot be avoided (e.g., graphs or screenshots).
procedure:
Using the mouse, click and drag over all text on the page to select it.
HTML text will be selectable. Text that is part of an image will show the entire image being highlighted.
Confirm that text is presented using text rather than in an image of text, except for logos and within pictures where it cannot be avoided (e.g., graphs or screenshots).
outcomes:
Pass =images of text are not used

Fail = images of text are used
method: Reliably distinguishing a genuine image of text from a photo, icon, or diagram requires visual/OCR judgment beyond what alt-text or filename heuristics can determine with confidence.

title: Captions & Audio Description
expectation: All video (both live AND prerecorded) content MUST include accurate captions. IF video content provides any information visually that is not described by an accompanying audio track, it MUST also include an Audio Description track that fully explains the visual information.
procedure: Confirm that all video content (live AND prerecorded) provides accurate captions via an accessible mechanism. IF video content provides any information visually that is not described by an accompanying audio track, it MUST also include an Audio Description track that fully explains the visual information.
outcomes:
Pass = all video content has captions AND an audio description track if it is required

Fail = all video content does not have captions OR it does not have a required audio description track
method: Detects <video> elements and checks for a <track kind="captions"> child; flags visual-only video without an accompanying <track kind="descriptions">. Judging caption/description accuracy is manual. Native videos with no declared track are played muted for ~1.5s so JavaScript players can expose caption text tracks; embedded YouTube/Vimeo players are queried for their caption tracks (flagging none, or auto-generated only).

title: Ways to Provide CC and AD
requirement: Ways to Provide CC and AD (VIS-4-2)
expectation:
Captions and Audio Description MUST be made available to users via one or more of the following methods (both need not use the same method): 
• always on, included in the original video
• included as a separate file or track that can be toggled on and off by the user via an accessible mechanism (note: use of Extended Audio Description may complicate this)
• included as a video file and made available via separate link(s) adjacent to the original video link
procedure:
Captions and Audio Description MUST be made available to users via one or more of the following methods (both need not use the same method):
always on, included in the original video(open captions)
included as a separate file or track tha can be toggled on and off by the user via an accessible mechanism (note: use of Extended Audio Description may complicate this)
included as a video file and made available via a separate link(s) adjacent to the original video link
outcomes:
Pass = captions and audio descriptions are made available through an accessible method

Fail = captions and audio descriptions are not made available through an accessible method
method: Checks whether detected video elements expose a caption track, an open-caption note, or an adjacent link plausibly toggling captions. Embedded YouTube/Vimeo players are queried for available caption tracks.

title: Transcripts for audio-only/video-only
expectation: For audio-only and video-only media, a transcript MUST be provided which provides the same information as presented in the original media content.
procedure: A transcript which provides the same information as presented in the original media content MUST be made available for all audio-only AND/OR video-only content.
outcomes:
Pass = transcripts are provided

Fail = transcripts are not provided

NA = no audio or video only content is present
method: Detects <audio> elements and video-only content, then checks for a nearby link/text containing "transcript".
